# Verification analysis: ipsec-site-tunnel-rhel7

Job: `2026-09-05__12-23-47`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node3` sits behind `node1` on `lan-a` and `node4` sits behind `node2` on
> `lan-b`. The two firewalls share a transit network, while the private
> networks have no path between them. Build an IPsec tunnel between `node1`
> and `node2` and carry the private networks over it, so `node3` and `node4`
> reach each other by their private addresses with that traffic encrypted in
> transit.

## Environment

- Systems: **2 opnsense + 2 rhel7.9**
- Networks: **mgmt, transit, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node3**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

The verifier treated the recorded trial as a full success. All requested outcomes were conclusively supported by the cited evidence.

The job contains **1 trial**, completed in **21m 45s** with **0 Harbor-reported errored trials** and **0 retries**.

## Trial `ipsec-site-tunnel-rhel7__YGiYk4k`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built a functioning IKEv2/PSK IPsec tunnel between node1 and node2 over the transit network, correctly carrying the 172.16.1.0/24 and 172.16.2.0/24 private subnets, and directly demonstrated encrypted end-to-end connectivity between node3 and node4 with a concurrent tcpdump showing only ESP traffic on the transit link. All four nodes were taken through a full restart cycle with pre-restart baseline, boot-identity change, and post-restart recovery of IPsec SAs and connectivity, including a legitimate mid-protocol fix for non-persistent RHEL7 interface addressing on node3. Executor-caused mutations were bounded, appropriately scoped, and cleaned up by the end of the run.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.900 | 132/12 (+7 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1-ipsec-tunnel — Satisfied:** Build an IPsec tunnel between node1 and node2 over the transit network
  - **Why:** swanctl --list-sas on both node1 and node2 shows IKE_SA ESTABLISHED (IKEv2, PSK auth) and CHILD_SA INSTALLED (TUNNEL mode, ESP:AES_GCM_16-128) between 10.255.255.1 and 10.255.255.2 on the transit link, with matching SPI pairs on both sides confirming a live, mutually-agreed tunnel.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-4f0a33e48199434a`, `cmd-cdff6fa7088e4994`
- **req-2-private-network-transport — Satisfied:** Carry node3's private network (behind node1) and node4's private network (behind node2) over the tunnel so they can reach each other by private address
  - **Why:** Traffic selectors on the CHILD_SA are 172.16.1.0/24 <-> 172.16.2.0/24, matching node3/node4's private subnets. Bidirectional ping from node3 (172.16.1.10) to node4 (172.16.2.10) and back succeeded with 0% packet loss.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-87a8c0dfbce74ccc`, `cmd-179997824793412e`, `cmd-ef548d8812464ba6`
- **req-3-encryption-in-transit — Satisfied:** Ensure traffic between the private networks is encrypted in transit (not exposed on the shared transit network)
  - **Why:** A tcpdump capture on node1's transit interface (vtnet1), running concurrently with the node3->node4 ping test, shows only ESP packets between 10.255.255.1 and 10.255.255.2 with no plaintext ICMP or private-address traffic visible on the wire.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-3122854d18a042ff`, `cmd-c301a50b7ebc43fa`, `cmd-ef548d8812464ba6`
- **req-4-node1-restart — Satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node1 pre-restart baseline, restart, and recovered state
  - **Why:** Pre-restart boot time (17:13:17) and healthy IPsec SA captured, reboot acknowledged, node unreachable during the transition, then reachable with a changed boot time (17:29:21). Post-restart evidence shows interfaces up, IPsec SA re-ESTABLISHED, and node3->node4 ping succeeding.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-1226f68b6ad34d45`, `cmd-62ece1b4d9f644e7`, `cmd-86d5113c26c244e4`, `cmd-251c0a88794f4a22`, `cmd-7bc62c04d3194707`, `cmd-73b5b53076964ffb`
- **req-5-node2-restart — Satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node2 pre-restart baseline, restart, and recovered state
  - **Why:** Pre-restart boot time (17:13:17) captured, reboot acknowledged, node unreachable then reachable with changed boot time (17:30:00). Post-restart shows IPsec SA re-ESTABLISHED and node4->node3 ping succeeding.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e6facc8261974061`, `cmd-ead48cc48f4a414a`, `cmd-53f29ed4a3fa49cc`, `cmd-9f705d75fb684c08`, `cmd-e73a5daf34124bd4`, `cmd-9ac343addafd45a0`
- **req-6-node3-restart — Satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node3 pre-restart baseline, restart, and recovered state
  - **Why:** Pre-restart boot_id (3dba43a5...) captured, reboot acknowledged, node unreachable then reachable with a new boot_id (74193578...). Private IP/route on eth1 did not survive reboot (ephemeral ip-command config); executor corrected this with persistent ifcfg-eth1/route-eth1 files, then confirmed recovery via successful node3->node4 ping.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Executor mutations were generally scoped, necessary, and cleaned up. Diagnostic IP addresses (172.31.99.3/24, 172.31.98.4/24) were assigned to node3/node4 eth1 for bridge/ARP topology discovery (cmd-45dcbbe0d53d47be, cmd-81833d071314469a) before final addressing was applied; this was a bounded, low-risk mutation that was subsequently overwritten by the production address via an explicit flush (cmd-fd02f0665e9446a6), so it left no residue. The generated PSK was briefly displayed in plaintext via cat (cmd-71f93f45eaa04054) but the corresponding temp file was deleted at the end of the run (cmd-9b18fef64ae24052, cmd-0722abbb4de241f2), along with tcpdump capture files and reboot logs across all four nodes (cmd-c7d64723bb05474f, cmd-3e0d4d59986443fc, cmd-300bc4d78f7d4b75, cmd-283414e01cb3410c). No firewall rules were left overly permissive (rules scoped to specific peer addresses/protocols on the transit interface), and no failed or conflicting services were left running. The node3/node4 eth1 addressing initially used non-persistent ip addr add commands, a design gap surfaced only during the restart test and then corrected with persistent ifcfg files -- functionally fine, though ideally applied from the start rather than discovered via the restart check.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-45dcbbe0d53d47be`, `cmd-81833d071314469a`, `cmd-fd02f0665e9446a6`, `cmd-71f93f45eaa04054`, `cmd-9b18fef64ae24052`, `cmd-0722abbb4de241f2`, `cmd-c7d64723bb05474f`, `cmd-3e0d4d59986443fc`, `cmd-300bc4d78f7d4b75`, `cmd-283414e01cb3410c`, `cmd-a1fe586efd684149`

### Comments and limitations

- The initial ephemeral ip addr add addressing approach on node3/node4 meant persistence was not verified until the restart test surfaced it, so the task's addressing design had a latent gap that was corrected reactively rather than proactively for node3.
- Package-manager-health checks were unavailable (timed out) for node3 and node4 in both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so package/dependency integrity could not be independently cross-checked.
- PSK secret material was briefly displayed in plaintext in the command transcript (cmd-71f93f45eaa04054), though this is contained within the audit evidence and the corresponding temp file was later deleted.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
